code2020.title: Ordonnance n° 2020-356 du 8 avril 2020 portant révision du Code électoral
code2020.note: Text layer. Title II sets each election: the president (Art. 43-64), deputies (Art. 65-103), senators (Art. 104-144), regional councillors (Art. 145-173), and municipal councillors (Art. 174-202). Art. 205 lists the laws it amends, starting with Law 2000-514 of 1 August 2000, the electoral code of 2000.

classes.name: Election du Président de la République
classes.locator: https://www.cei.ci/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Ordonnance-N%C2%B0-2020-356-portant-Nouveau-Code-%C3%A9lectoral-du-08-Avr.2020.pdf (Art. 43-45: five-year term, absolute majority or a runoff between the top two, first round on the last Saturday of October)
classes.note: Elected directly since independence: single candidates in 1960-1985, contested since 1990. The 2010 election went to a runoff. The 2016 Constitution created a vice president, appointed rather than elected since the 2020 revision; no vice president has been elected on a ticket. The CEI's site holds results from 2010; 1960-2000 results sit in Supreme Court and Constitutional Council decisions that are not online.

classes.name: Election des députés à l'Assemblée nationale
classes.locator: https://www.cei.ci/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Ordonnance-N%C2%B0-2020-356-portant-Nouveau-Code-%C3%A9lectoral-du-08-Avr.2020.pdf (Art. 67-69: five-year term; one-round plurality, single-member seats by candidate and multi-member seats by closed winner-take-all list; circumscriptions set by decree)
classes.note: Unicameral until the Senate first sat in 2018. A single national list until 1975, competing single-party candidates in 1980 and 1985, and multiparty contests since 1990. 255 seats in 205 circumscriptions since 2011. The 1959 Legislative Assembly of the autonomous republic preceded it. The CEI's site holds results from 2011; earlier ones are not online.

classes.name: Election des conseillers généraux
classes.note: Departments were local governments with elected general councils from 2002, elected once in July 2002; the 2011-2012 reform kept only regions and communes.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes the July 2002 general-council results online: the CEI's site and media library start with 2010, and the Constitutional Council's online decisions start in 2020.

classes.name: Gouverneur et conseil de district autonome
classes.locator: https://www.cei.ci/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Ordonnance-N%C2%B0-2020-356-portant-Nouveau-Code-%C3%A9lectoral-du-08-Avr.2020.pdf (Art. 109: elected district councillors sit in the senatorial college)
classes.note: Abidjan and Yamoussoukro are run by governors appointed by decree; the electoral code provides no popular vote for the district council or governor (Art. 1 lists only the presidential, legislative, senatorial, regional, and municipal elections).
classes.disposition_reason: No popular election: governors are appointed and the electoral code (Art. 1) holds no district ballot.

classes.name: Conseil général et Assemblée territoriale de la Côte d'Ivoire
classes.note: The colony's General Council (1946) and Territorial Assembly (1952, 1957), elected under French law; the 1957 assembly became the constituent and then legislative assembly of the autonomous republic in December 1958.
classes.disposition_reason: Results appear only in the colonial Journal officiel, which no Ivorian official body publishes online.

classes.name: Députés et sénateurs de la Côte d'Ivoire au Parlement français
classes.name_en: Members of the French Parliament for Côte d'Ivoire (1945-1958)
classes.disposition_reason: Elections to the French National Assembly and Council of the Republic belong to the France census, as does the 1958 referendum.

classes.name: Primaires
classes.locator: https://www.cei.ci/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Ordonnance-N%C2%B0-2020-356-portant-Nouveau-Code-%C3%A9lectoral-du-08-Avr.2020.pdf (Art. 51-53: presidential candidates file with the CEI and need citizen sponsorship (parrainage), not a primary)
classes.disposition_reason: The state runs no nominating contest: parties pick their candidates, and the presidential sponsorship of Art. 51 is a signature requirement, not a vote.
